data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Sadid" carries a powerful meaning in the context of Islamic culture. In Islamic society, being a Sadid or a helper and supporter is highly valued. Those who provide aid, assistance, and support to their fellow Muslims are held in high esteem. The name symbolizes the communal and interconnected nature of Islamic society, where one's actions and support have a direct impact on others.
data.spiritual_significance: At its heart, the Islamic name "Sadid" represents the spiritual principle of compassion, kindness, and selflessness. In Islamic teachings, helping others, providing aid and support, and caring for the weak and vulnerable are important acts of worship. By carrying the name Sadid, one is reminded of the spiritual responsibility to support and help others, both within their immediate community and beyond, and to embody the compassionate and selfless qualities that the name represents. Ultimately, the name serves as a constant reminder of the importance of supporting and uplifting others both spiritually and materially, and of the profound impact that small acts of kindness and support can have on the world around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Support, Help, Aid" symbolizes One who provides support and aid, a helper and supporter. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Sadid serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of support, help, aid.

historical_references.reference: Sadid al-Din Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Qunawi, a Persian Sufi scholar and philosopher. He was a student of Ibn al-Arabi and is known for his works on Sufi philosophy and metaphysics. He lived during the 13th century.

Sadid al-Din Mohammad, a Mughal emperor who ruled India in the late 15th century. He succeeded the emperor Sikandar Lodhi and was known for his military conquests and patronage of the arts. He is also known as Adil Shah and is considered the founder of the Suri Dynasty.
